summary: New Settings -> Backup & Recovery 'Configuration backup' panel and a first-run wizard recovery step that export and restore a portable, passphrase-encrypted .mmbackup of the app's configuration, so a fresh install can be brought up without reconfiguring. The bundle covers four independently selectable sections: Cameras (camera + ONVIF rows including stored credentials + recording configs), AI Detection (detection rules + the detection-class registry), Notifications (destinations + delivery settings, including Telegram/webhook/MQTT secrets), and App Settings (decoder/vision/capture + camera-health + machine-health). Because the file carries plaintext secrets that the normal API strips (json:"-" camera passwords, notification tokens), the engine reads entity rows directly and the whole file is encrypted with a user passphrase via a new portable Argon2id+AES-256-GCM primitive (infra/atrest.EncryptWithPassphrase/DecryptWithPassphrase) that is NOT tied to the machine's at-rest key, so a backup made on one host opens on another. Endpoints: GET /api/settings/backup/sections (row counts), POST /api/settings/backup/export|preview|restore (base64-in-JSON, admin-gated). Restore remaps auto-assigned primary keys (cameras insert first and build an old->new id map; recording configs, ONVIF rows and AI rules re-point to the new camera id; rules whose camera was not restored are skipped and counted), upserts the detection-class registry by name, and upserts settings by key; Replace mode wipes the selected sections first, Merge appends. The setup wizard's welcome step gains a 'Restore from backup' branch (upload + passphrase -> replace-restore -> restart to apply).
compatibility: Fully backward compatible and purely additive: no database schema changes (all data already exists as rows/key-values), no config changes. NewBackupService/NewBackupApi are new and wired in app.go using the existing repositories; no existing constructor signatures change. Machine identity is intentionally never included in a backup (the at-rest key, node pairing/enrollment, mTLS certificates, config.json, and the setup-complete flag), so restoring onto a second machine does not clone identity. Custom AI model .pt weights are referenced but not embedded in v1. Local user accounts are out of scope for v1 (deferred). The backup file is only as strong as its passphrase (minimum 8 characters), which cannot be recovered if lost.
